message.content:
**Round 1 — Claude Fable 5.1**

**A) Agenda**

**Q1 — Part A.** Seal it, with three amendments. The formula is the standard Treasury BEY for bills ≤ 182 days; 91 fixed days is fine (actual maturities vary ±1–2 days, effect < 0.5 bp). Convert both TB3MS and DTB3; never splice GS3M — a splice puts a 0.08 pp level break at 1981-09 (E1's instrument/fitting difference) into the one series the model reads. Amendment 1: disclose that BEY(mean of daily d) ≠ mean of daily BEY(d) (Jensen; convexity of the formula), and compute the daily DTB3 version as mean-of-converted so the live input matches the pinned procedure; quantify the monthly-average bias once on 1954–2026 and print it. Amendment 2: preregister the arithmetic as well as the skill prediction: at d ≈ 4 %, gap 0.10 pp → ΔP ≈ −1.6 pp at today's input; at the 1980–81 inversions (d 12–15 %) the discount curve is overstated by 0.55–0.81 pp, i.e. inversions were *deeper* than the model saw. I accept |Δ walk-forward| < 2 pp as the preregistered band but expect a small positive sign (deeper 1970s–80s inversions, less steep 1980s recoveries); write the sign down so it cannot be claimed afterwards. Is the convention a defect? Yes, a measurement defect, but a self-consistent one: the weights were estimated on the same mismeasured series, so P today is internally coherent. It is not worth breaking the frozen weights or §1.3 over ~1.6 pp; the unscored sensitivity is the right instrument, and the switch decision belongs to the 2027 refit council. Post hoc status: the issue surfaced from a review of today's reading, but the sensitivity cannot touch P — acceptable.

**Q2 — Part B.** B3 only, but Claude's justification is the wrong one and the spec must say so. The EBP analogy is weak: EBP was closed because its *onset pattern* was seen; the step-4 ACM test, by Claude's own admission, never isolated the expectations hypothesis — it measured a missing-history penalty. The decisive argument is power, not contamination: a common panel from 1961Q3 with 8 onsets gives MDE80 ≈ 30 pp of skill, so B1/B2 would return "no difference" whatever the truth, and a result that cannot inform a decision should not be run — not even as a declared second shot. The spec must state verbatim: "E3's −77.88 pp is a result on an implementation, not on the hypothesis; it is not evidence against the expectations component." Otherwise a future council will cite the number as a rejection. For B3: the context line prints *both* estimates (KW daily, ACM monthly-lagged) with their dates, not THREEFYTP10 alone — E2 shows a 0.15 pp disagreement between them on a 1.0 pp curve. The ≥ 12-snapshot revision audit: archive the full ACMTP10/THREEFYTP10 series monthly, report max |revision| of each month's TP over the trailing 24 months across vintages; the unscored column opens only if the audited revision is < 10 bp, which the spec pins now.

**Q3 — C5/C6.** C5: amend one sentence. "The gap (0.18pp) is convention, not data" is wrong by E1's own arithmetic: at d = 4.04, the convention gap is 0.10 pp; the remaining 0.08 pp is DGS3MO vs converted DTB3 — different instruments and curve fitting. Text: "Of the 0.18pp gap, 0.10pp is the discount→BEY convention; 0.08pp is instrument/fitting (DGS3MO vs DTB3). Neither is data error." C6: amend harder than Claude proposes. As written it is a directional claim on P — "the predictive part of the curve is ~0, so P is understated" — sourced from one term-structure model on one day, with the literature cited as authority. No other context line (EBP, Sahm, claims) carries a "the literature says this predicts recessions" sentence; C6 should not either. Strike the Rosenberg-Maurer sentence and the "98 %" framing; fix the rejection sentence. Text: "Curve decomposition (model-dependent, revised ex post): KW 2026-10-16 TP 0.99, expectations 4.10; ACM 2026-07 TP 0.84 (0.51 in 2026-06). The model reads only the sum. A feature using the ACM-adjusted curve was tested in step 4; the result (−77.9pp) measured mainly the pre-1961 panel penalty, not the hypothesis. Closed list; prospective proposal in spec2027/udkast/7. Not in P." The firewall is only honest if context lines are numbers, not arguments.

**Q4 — C1–C4, C7.** C1–C4: ratify ex post. 5 bp is post hoc and cosmetic; any threshold in 2–10 bp would have relabelled today's +1.4 bp, it cannot move P, and 5 bp ≈ 0.8 pp of P is a sensible "indistinguishable from noise" scale — disclose and keep. C7: amend. Printing the 198-origin paired-loss interval (+0.120 nats, +27.1 %) directly under the §1.2 sentence gives the oracle-censored figure the only uncertainty band on the page, so the eye reads +27 % [−4; +24 nats-equivalent] as the headline — a §1.2-spirit breach even if the sentence order is kept. Fix: compute the same episode-block paired bootstrap (1000 draws, seed 42, cycle blocks) on the oracle-free 219-origin set and print both intervals in §1.2 order; this is a diagnostic on existing predictions, touches nothing frozen, and is acceptable pre-refit. Until it exists, label the 198 interval "oracle-censored set; oracle-free interval pending". Also add the plain fact: lower bound < 0, 8.9 % of draws ≤ 0 — one-sided p ≈ 0.09 with 9 blocks; the historical skill is not robust at conventional levels and the dashboard should say so. The gate line "F5 +23.2 % vs curve-only +27.1 %" must carry "(oracle-censored full path; oracle-free headline +20.37 %)".

**Q5 — verdict wording.** Leave it. "No robust signal under the band rule" is a *different* claim — it reads as "nothing is happening", whereas "not distinguishable from the base rate" correctly says the model cannot separate 14.8 % from 18 % (2007Q4 read 16.7 %, same verdict, onset next month). Keep the paired supplement visible whenever it disagrees, with the 12/198 historical disagreement rate stated; the ledger key is not amended.

**B) Verdict on Claude's draft positions**

- Q1: keep, amended (Jensen/mean-of-converted; preregistered sign + ΔP ≈ −1.6 pp arithmetic).
- Q2: keep B3; strike the EBP-analogy justification, replace with power + non-isolation; add the verbatim E3 disclaimer; both TP estimates in the context line; pin the 10 bp revision criterion.
- Q3: amend C5 (0.10 convention / 0.08 instrument); C6 — strike R-M sentence and 98 %, rewrite the step-4 sentence as above. Claude's amendment keeps the two elements that make it a directional signal.
- Q4: ratify C1–C4; amend C7 (oracle-free 219-origin interval first; gate line label; p ≈ 0.09 stated).
- Q5: keep.

**C) Biggest risk in my proposal**

Stripping C6 to numbers removes the one fact a reader of a curve-only model most needs today: that the +1.1 pp curve is almost entirely term premium, and that on the best available literature the model is reading the wrong component. If an onset arrives in 2027 behind a flat expectations curve and a 15 % P, the record will show that the council chose a tidy firewall over a true warning. I accept that risk because the alternative — a context line that argues P is wrong, from a revisable model, without a test that can ever be scored on fewer than two post-sealing onsets — is exactly the unvalidated side-channel the firewall was written to exclude.
message.reasoning:
I'm drafting a Round 1 independent proposal as a senior macro-econometrician, aiming to be concrete and quantitative while pushing back hard on Opus's draft positions. Starting with Q1, I'm working through the bond-equivalent yield conversion formula for a 13-week Treasury bill and checking the standard day-count convention.

Converting TB3MS's monthly average discount rate directly versus averaging daily-converted BEY values introduces a small Jensen's inequality bias worth disclosing, though it's negligible in magnitude. I favor converting both the calibration and live series to BEY rather than splicing at 1981, since a splice would introduce a level break, and the CMT cross-check showing roughly 0.08pp instrument difference post-1981 supports this. I'm framing the operational convention as a genuine defect — a level-dependent measurement inconsistency that needs to be flagged.

Since the fitted weights were estimated on the discount-basis curve, the calibration stays internally consistent even though the discount convention overstated the true curve by 0.4-0.8pp during the high-rate 70s-80s period; given that 1980-81 inversions were already deeply negative, this distortion likely has minimal effect on classification. Today's sensitivity (~0.10pp at 4% rates, translating to roughly -1.6pp in P) isn't material enough to warrant touching the frozen weights, so I'd leave the unscored sensitivity check as adequate. On the sign of the prediction's effect, I genuinely can't call it confidently — the convention could make 70s-80s inversions deeper while flattening the 1980s recoveries, so I'll just note the prediction holds without committing to a direction.

Minor additional checks: the paired bootstrap setup with 1000 draws and seed 42 seems fine as is, Brier scoring isn't necessary to add, and the oracle-free headline/ordering rule in Part A is already handled correctly. The pre-1953 Shiller monthly-average rate versus CMT discrepancy isn't relevant here. I'd flag that this whole convention question only surfaces as a post-hoc concern because a reviewer noticed today's ~1.6pp effect — worth acknowledging that framing.

For Part B, I partly disagree with Opus: EBP §8.2 was closed based on an observed historical onset pattern, but the expectations component's step-4 test was really dominated by the missing-history penalty, meaning the hypothesis was never truly isolated — which Claude itself admits. The forking-paths concern is real, but the literature direction was already known for every feature on the closed list (Sahm, claims, etc.), so the actual contamination source seems to be the 2023 false alarm and the known Rosenberg-Maurer result rather than genuine data snooping. I'm leaning toward treating this as B3 only, or explicitly declaring it a second shot, though I want to think through that further.

The step-4 test result of −77.9 pp tells us nothing about the hypothesis, and the closed-list status is just procedural. The real issue is power: a second test on the smaller 1961– panel with only 8 onsets would have an MDE around 30 pp, meaning it's almost guaranteed to show "no difference" simply because it has essentially zero power to detect anything — so B1/B2 is pointless regardless of contamination concerns. That makes B3 the right call, though I should flag that the unscored ledger column needs a ≥12-snapshot revision audit of ACMTP10/KW — storing monthly vintages and computing the maximum TP revision over the trailing 24 months across those vintages.

I agree with the choice of THREEFYTP10 for context, but since KW daily and ACM monthly disagree by 0.15 pp on term premium, both should be shown in the context line rather than picking one — the Q2 context line should print both estimates and state the range. I also need the spec to explicitly record that Part B is closed historically and that the −77.9 figure is a non-isolating test result, not evidence against the hypothesis, so no future reviewer misreads it as a rejection.

On C5, the gap figure is imprecise: of the 0.18pp gap, 0.10 is convention and the remaining 0.08 is instrument/curve-fitting difference — I should amend C5 to reflect that split rather than attributing the whole gap to convention.

C6 is the real problem for the firewall — saying "98% of the curve is term premium" alongside the expectations-component literature effectively signals to the reader that the premium estimate is too low, since a near-zero expectations component implies the market isn't pricing rate cuts.

I should keep C6 consistent with the other context lines—just numbers, no interpretive framing—so I'd cut the R-M sentence and the 98% figure, noting instead that no validated test isolates this claim in the model. Same issue with the ACM-rejection line: it should be reframed as "tested in step 4; result (−77.9pp) measured mainly the panel [effect]" rather than implying outright rejection of the idea.

On Q4's threshold items: C1's 5bp cutoff set after observing 1.4bp is post hoc but defensible with disclosure, and I could anchor it to something less arbitrary like the daily std or a dP equivalent (~0.8pp). C2-C4 can be ratified as-is, though C4's timing math (quarter end + 32 + 10 days) needs checking against the actual BEA advance release lag of ~28-30 days.

For C7, I'm noticing that printing the oracle-censored +27.1% figure with its confidence interval under §1.2's sentence gives it more visual prominence than the oracle-free +20.37% headline, which lacks an interval entirely — that's a violation of §1.2's spirit. I should amend C7 to compute the paired loss bootstrap for the oracle-free 219-origin set too, and print that one first.

I also realize the gate line comparing F5 to the curve-only figure uses the oracle-censored +27.1% standalone, which also needs labeling to clarify it's on the oracle-censored path alongside the oracle-free headline — this is an acceptable diagnostic since it doesn't alter the underlying predictions pre-refit, just needs the label amended.

Since the 90% interval lower bound (−0.042) crosses zero, the historical skill isn't significant at 10% two-sided (one-sided p≈0.089), and I should state this plainly, also flagging that the 9-block bootstrap is coarse and limits interval credibility. For Q5, I'll keep "not distinguishable" in the ledger but add a one-line dashboard explainer clarifying the verdict rule is band-based, since "no robust signal" alone could be misread as "nothing happening."

The paired supplement (more permissive, using 12/198 historical origins) says "below base rate" today but never overrides the verdict — that's already handled, so the fix is just making sure this disagreement flag always displays when the two rules diverge. I'll leave Q5's wording as-is and reject review 1's "no robust signal" phrasing since it's a stronger claim than "not distinguishable from base rate."

For the other questions: Q4 holds — at 16.7%, the model is honestly low-power and correctly flags it as indistinguishable before onset. On verdicts overall, I'll keep Q1 with amendments (adding the Jensen note, sign-free prediction, and the preregistered ΔP arithmetic), keep Q2's B3 but broaden the justification beyond contamination to include power issues and show both KW and ACM results, amend Q3's C5 and C6 (stripping the R-M sentence and the 98% figure), ratify Q4's C1–C4 while amending C7, and leave Q5 untouched. The biggest risk I see is that my C6 amendment might strip out a true and relevant piece of information in the process.

Weighing the risks, removing the C6 sentence about the curve being mostly term premium could look like suppression if a recession hits in 2027 with a flat expectations curve — that's worse than the scope-creep risk from introducing a new oracle-free bootstrap computation in C7, so I'll go with C6 as the one to flag. Now I need to keep the whole write-up tight, around 1200 words.
